content:
Cook is visiting Apple's Battersea campus in London this week to meet with King Charles III, as part of a new partnership between the company and The King's Trust.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down for an exclusive interview with The Independent, diving deep into the partnership and his first month as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO last month, handing the role over to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook noted that the transition "really started a few years ago."

Ternus steps into the CEO role as the iPhone Duo launches, a product Cook says was planned long in advance. "I wanted John to step into a tailwind, and a big part of Apple's tailwind is the product cycle," he explained.

Cook also emphasised that his focus as executive chairman is on "global policy" and pointed to the "very high level of trust" between him and Ternus. Though Cook is available to help Ternus "in whatever way he deems appropriate," he stressed that he is "not overstepping."

What advice did Cook give Ternus? "Don't try to be me." The full interview is available at The Independent, with a detailed look at the new partnership between Apple and The King's Trust.
